input: Set up a donor-advised fund for charitable giving

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Whether they want end-to-end help (choosing a sponsor, opening the account, funding it, and making grants) or just one specific phase changes the entire plan.
A DAF for an individual has different setup steps than one for a family, business, or estate — it affects account structure, named advisors, and succession planning.
The initial contribution size determines which sponsoring organisations are eligible (some have minimums of $5K, others $25K+) and which investment options are available.
Whether there is a tax deadline, a triggering event (e.g. a business sale, bonus, inheritance), or no time pressure changes how urgently each step must be completed.

Some sponsors (Fidelity Charitable, Schwab, Vanguard Charitable, community foundations) differ in fees, investment options, grant minimums, and values alignment — knowing priorities shapes the recommendation.
The asset type being contributed (cash, appreciated stock, real estate, private business interests) directly determines which sponsors can accept it and the complexity of the transfer process.
Understanding whether success means the account is simply open, fully funded, or already making grants to specific causes clarifies what 'done' looks like and sets the right endpoint for the plan.

gold.taskTitle: Set up a donor-advised fund for charitable giving
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to establish a donor-advised fund (DAF) to organise and direct charitable contributions.

questions.title: Which phases of the process do you need help with?
questions.description: Clarify whether the user needs guidance on choosing a sponsor, opening the account, funding it, making grants, or the entire end-to-end process.

questions.title: Is this DAF for you alone or a family or business?
questions.description: Determine whether the DAF is for an individual, a couple, a multi-generational family, or a corporate giving programme, as this affects account structure and succession.

questions.title: What is the approximate size of your initial contribution?
questions.description: Identify the intended opening contribution amount to filter sponsors by minimum requirements and appropriate investment tiers.

questions.title: Is there a tax year deadline or triggering event driving this?
questions.description: Establish whether a liquidity event, year-end tax deadline, or other time-sensitive trigger is shaping when the DAF must be open and funded.

questions.title: What matters most when choosing a sponsoring organisation?
questions.description: Understand the user's priorities — low fees, investment flexibility, values alignment, community foundation connection, brand reputation — to recommend the right sponsor.

questions.title: What type of asset will you contribute to fund the DAF?
questions.description: Determine whether the contribution will be cash, publicly traded stock, restricted stock, real estate, or private business interests, as this affects sponsor eligibility and transfer complexity.

questions.title: What does a successfully completed DAF look like to you?
questions.description: Define the finish line — whether success means the account is open, fully funded, invested, or actively making grants to identified causes.
